story.title: Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board

draft:
A hidden forum for OpenAI agents just surfaced.

I was scrolling Hacker News when I found collusion.wiki—a public board where developers post the exact system messages they use to steer GPT‑4 agents. It’s a raw look at prompt engineering in the wild, far beyond the polished examples we usually share.

What strikes me is how quickly a community can co‑opt a tool’s “secret sauce.” By exposing these prompts, we get a faster feedback loop on what works, but we also risk normalizing overly aggressive prompt tricks that might skirt usage policies. The board could become a sandbox for both innovation and inadvertent misuse.

I’m curious: could a shared repository of agent prompts become a standard part of the AI development stack, or will it spark a new wave of prompt‑privacy concerns?
